How to get your focus back
in a distracted world
Start your day without your phone. The first hour sets your attention for the whole day. Read, train or plan before you check a single notification.
Work in blocks of 45 minutes. One task, timer on, phone in another room. Short, protected sessions get more done than a whole distracted afternoon.
Turn off almost every notification. Keep calls and messages from close people. Everything else can wait until you decide to look.
Do one thing at a time, even when you relax. Watch the film without scrolling, eat without your phone. Focus is a habit you train all day long.
Feed your attention with something better. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and it trains my mind to stay on one thing.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It trains my mind to stay on one thing.

slides.texte_overlay: Get bored on purpose. Wait in line without your phone, walk without music. Your brain needs empty moments to recover its attention.
Sleep and move enough. Tired, inactive bodies can't focus well. Good sleep and daily exercise are the base of every sharp mind.
